name: Lovono
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Tryon, Darrell. 1994 (pp. 630-634): short grammatical account of Lovono (cited in François 2009, The languages of Vanikoro; François 2009 itself read — no stress statement)

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2022. Presentation of the Lovono language, and audio archive (corpus page with 'Notes on the language'). Pangloss Collection. Paris: CNRS-LACITO. https://pangloss.cnrs.fr/corpus/Lovono
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 3.1 Orthography gives 18 phonemic consonants (Table 1), 5 short vowels (Table 2), allophony of /v/ and /i/; nothing on stress, accent or prosody anywhere on the page.

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2021. Teanu dictionary: Introduction. Dictionaria 15. Leipzig: MPI-EVA. (with Lovono and Tanema equivalents)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 6.2 p. 11: 'Stress regularly hits the penultimate syllable of a phonological word' -- explicitly about TEANU; Lovono figures only as lexical equivalents (537 headwords) and in two example sentences, with no phonological statement of its own.

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2009. The languages of Vanikoro: Three lexicons and one grammar. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: Papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 103-126. Pacific Linguistics 605. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only fn. 7 (p. 107): the three Vanikoro languages share one phoneme inventory (5 short vowels, 19 consonants); sound-correspondence discussion in sect. 2.1; no statement on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/prosod: no hits).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for vano1237 (Lovono): classification, endangerment, links; subclassification refs Ross & Næss 2007, Næss & Boerger 2008, François 2009.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic pointers only. Grambank page for vano1237 (read online, not saved) cites François 2006, 2009, 2014 and Ray 1926 as its only sources.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. Grammar of the Vanikolo language. In A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages, Cambridge: CUP, pp. 455-461 (Rosetta Project excerpt, archive.org id rosettaproject_vnk_morsyn-1). Language identified as Lovono by its pronouns nane/ago/nani/gitu/gamitu/gaiva/detu, matching François's Lovono paradigm.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 1 'Alphabet' and 2 'Sounds' (p. 455) list letters and their values (from Fox, Ivens, Gaimard); no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. Unpublished Lovono field notes and recordings (2005, 2012; last speaker Rubenson Lono, d. 2020), archived in the Pangloss/Cocoon collection, and any future Lovono sketch by the same author.

sources.note: François is the only modern linguist to have worked on Lovono; his Teanu introduction gives penultimate stress and his Lovono corpus page repeats the Teanu phoneme tables without the stress paragraph, so any Lovono-specific stress statement would have to come from his data.
